_note: Loose family. The Semitic members (Punic, Akkadian, Ge'ez, Sabaean) share real cognate roots (mlk=king, baal=lord, qart=city); the Egyptian (Afro-Asiatic) sub-palette is related but distinct. All members are civ (feudal government). Base provides the concept inventory, morphology template, Semitic title roots, and sub-palette notes; each culture realizes its own phonology.

phonology.palette: Near-Eastern: emphatic and guttural consonants (q, kh, h, ', sh, ts), triconsonantal roots, a/i/u vowels; Egyptian adds dj/tj and -aa/-et.

sub_palette_notes.punic: Phoenician-Punic: b/d/g, ', sh, t; -t feminine; common/title roots melek/baal/qart (theophoric built on morphed canon-stems, never real theonyms).
sub_palette_notes.akkadian: Assyrian-Babylonian: sh, ', kh; -u/-tu endings; common/title roots sharru/bel/alu (theophoric built on morphed canon-stems, never real theonyms).
sub_palette_notes.egyptian: Old/New Kingdom: dj, tj, kh; -aa/-et endings; common/title roots per/nesut/heqa (theophoric built on morphed canon-stems, never real theonyms).

phonology.phonotactics: CVC common; triconsonantal stems; gutturals frequent; stress varies.

lexicon_concepts._note: Same concept inventory as the Classical base; realized per sub-palette in each culture kit.

shared_roots._note: Semitic cognates recognizable across the Semitic members (not Egyptian).

morphology_template.toponymic_suffixes: settlement = theophoric construct (Qart-X = city-of-X), or feature/founder + sub-palette suffix.
morphology_template.patronymic_form: patronymic particle (bin/bar/ben = son-of; Akkadian mar; Egyptian sa) or theophoric construct; clan/house for nobility.

title_ladder_structure._note: ACKS 7 tiers, feudal, rhyming ruler/domain. The Semitic members share the mlk root at the kingdom tier (melek/sharru/negus); Egyptian uses per-aa (pharaoh = the Great House). Tier->ruler-level mapping pending the ACKS lookup.

conventions.people_name_default: given name + patronymic (bin/bar/mar/sa) or theophoric construct; clan/house for nobility; order given-first.
conventions.transparent_vs_opaque: low-moderate; many names are opaque theophoric constructs.
